text.label: Shorter
text.instruction: Cut each slot to about two thirds of its length, and keep every fact.

text.label: Simpler words
text.instruction: Use shorter, everyday words and plain sentences a first-year student reads at a glance.

text.label: More personal
text.instruction: Speak to the reader as you, about their own week and choices.

text.label: More surprising
text.instruction: Lead with the fact the reader would least expect, and let the wording show why it surprises.

text.label: More practical
text.instruction: Turn each point into something the reader can do, with the step stated plainly.

text.label: Warmer
text.instruction: Sound kinder and closer, like a friend who has been there, without softening the facts.

image.label: Closer
image.instruction: Move in closer on the subject so it fills more of the frame.

image.label: Wider
image.instruction: Pull back to a wider view that shows more of the place around the subject.

image.label: More people
image.instruction: Show a few more people in the scene, going about their day.

image.label: Fewer things
image.instruction: Clear the scene: fewer objects, more open space around the subject.

image.label: Warmer light
image.instruction: Light the scene with warmer light, like late afternoon sun or a desk lamp.

image.label: Calmer
image.instruction: Make the scene calmer: slower, quieter, softer contrast and less going on.
